payload.statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. If x is a real number with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n, then t = n*x - j satisfies 0 <= t < 1 and x = T_{n,j}(t).

result_payload.proof_nl: Because j/n <= x < (j+1)/n and n is positive, multiplying the inequality by n preserves the order and gives j <= nx < j+1. Now set t = nx - j. Subtracting j from the displayed inequality yields 0 <= t < 1. Also nx = j + t, so dividing by n gives x = (j+t)/n. The affine reconstruction map on the cell [j/n,(j+1)/n) is exactly T_{n,j}(u) = (j+u)/n, hence x = T_{n,j}(t).
result_payload.proof_summary: Multiply the interval bounds by n to get j <= nx < j+1, then subtract j to obtain 0 <= t < 1. Rewriting nx = j+t gives x = (j+t)/n, which is the cell reconstruction T_{n,j}(t).
